catalog_metadata.purpose: Every current and proposed feature for a future intraday quantitative model. Analysis only -- no feature listed as 'available_today: false' has been implemented by this document.

schema_notes.available_today: true only if a working, cited code path computes this value today.
schema_notes.used_in_decision: true only if decision_engine.rules.classify() actually reads this value (directly or via composite_score) when producing BUY/WATCH/AVOID/EXIT/NO_ACTION.
schema_notes.training_safe: true only if, as currently computed, the value could be used as a training feature with no known look-ahead risk. false or 'unverified' where a real or unassessed risk exists.
schema_notes.leakage_risk: low | medium | high | unverified -- unverified means no leakage test has ever been run for this specific value (most 'proposed' features).
schema_notes.quality: high | medium | low | unknown -- unknown where the feature has never been exercised end-to-end (e.g. anything gated behind an intraday interval, since no workflow has ever used one).

features.source: market_intelligence/scanner.py:239-270, sector-average trailing return minus universe-average, computed internally over the SCANNED universe
features.notes: None if no sector_map supplied. Internally computed, NOT the same data as the external NIFTY sector indices in market_intelligence/regime.py -- a disclosed inconsistency between two 'sector strength' concepts in this codebase. Leakage risk medium: relies on market_intelligence/nse_sector_map.py, a static present-day lookup with no historical versioning -- a backtest could silently use today's sector classification for a historical date.

features.source: market_intelligence/scanner.py:274-280, equal-weighted (1.0 each) sum of trend_score+momentum_score+breakout_score+relative_strength_score+sector_strength_score

features.source: decision_engine/confidence.py:52-88, fraction of 5 CandidateScore sub-scores agreeing in sign with composite_score
features.notes: Explicitly documented in its own source as NOT calibrated to historical outcomes. Shape looks like a probability (0.0-1.0); substance is a same-bar factor-agreement heuristic. Not read by classify() (computed after the label). Should not be used as a training label or feature implying a real probability without recalibration.

features.source: PROPOSED -- does not exist anywhere in market/indicators.py today, despite being an LLM prompt text field (schemas/technical.py::TechnicalAnalysis.vwap: str)
features.notes: A confirmed, real gap -- VWAP is referenced in the roadmap's worked example and asked of the LLM, but never computed as a number anywhere. Requires intraday bars and a session-reset convention (VWAP must reset each trading session, not roll continuously) that does not exist in this codebase today.

features.source: PROPOSED -- no reusable gap FEATURE exists; the only 'gap' concept in the codebase is predictions/tracker.py's ANOMALOUS_BAR_GAP_THRESHOLD, a data-quality GUARD, not a feature
features.notes: Must be carefully distinguished from a genuine corporate-action-driven price jump (which the existing anomaly guard exists to catch) -- a naive gap feature risks conflating real overnight gaps with unadjusted-split artifacts.

features.notes: Recommended primary ML target in TRADING_INTELLIGENCE_GAP_ANALYSIS.md. Leakage risk MEDIUM specifically because of the overlapping-label problem: consecutive/near-consecutive signals for the same symbol produce overlapping, non-independent outcome windows, which would silently invalidate any Wilson/normal-approximation CI computed over them unless explicitly addressed (non-overlapping sampling or a weighting scheme) -- a named, unresolved risk in the companion document.
